• ACUTAAS (Dividend): Here's an executive summary of the document: Executive Summary: Acutaas Chemicals Limited has declared a final dividend of Rs. 2.50 per share for FY 2025-26, which, under the newly effective Income-tax Act, 2025, is now taxable at the shareholder's end requiring mandatory Tax Deducted at Source (TDS). Shareholders must proactively submit specific tax-related documents by September 15, 2026, to ensure application of the correct or lower withholding tax rates. Failure to do so will result in higher default TDS, placing a significant administrative burden and immediate financial impact on shareholders, particularly non-residents navigating complex Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) provisions, and potentially requiring them to claim refunds later. └ 📄 Source

• AKSHARCHEM (Dividend): Aksharchem (India) Limited has notified shareholders of its 37th Annual General Meeting on September 22, 2026, providing online access to the FY2025-26 Annual Report and sending physical notices to those without registered emails. Materially, the Board has recommended a ₹0.50 per equity share dividend for FY2025-26, subject to AGM approval, and is urging shareholders to update KYC details to facilitate electronic dividend payments and enhance digital communication. No immediate red flags are identified; the document primarily concerns routine regulatory compliance and shareholder engagement. └ 📄 Source

• AKSHARCHEM (Dividend): Aksharchem (India) Limited reported a challenging FY 2025-26, incurring a net loss of ₹43.86 lakhs and a 2.16% EBITDA decline, primarily due to rising input costs, geopolitical headwinds, and US tariffs, despite a 7.5% increase in total income. The company responded by strategically investing in long-term resilience, including a 50% expansion of Precipitated Silica capacity to 18,000 MTPA and a 7.93 MWp solar power installation, positioning itself for future growth in specialty chemicals despite the current profitability setback. └ 📄 Source

No immediate red flags are present, as this appears to be a standard regulatory announcement for a significant shareholder distribution. └ 📄 Source

• AMBIKCO (Dividend): Here's an executive summary of the document: Ambika Cotton Mills Limited's Annual General Meeting notice for FY 2025-26 reveals the company's robust financial health, proposing the adoption of audited statements and a significant final dividend of Rs. 37 per equity share. A key takeaway and potential area for scrutiny is the proposed re-appointment of the 77-year-old Managing Director for another five years, alongside the continued tenure or appointment of three other directors aged 75 or above, all requiring special resolutions under SEBI regulations. • AMRUTANJAN (Dividend): Amrutanjan Health Care Limited reported strong FY2026 performance with 11% revenue growth and 25% profit before tax growth (before exceptional items), primarily propelled by its Pain Management and Women's Hygiene segments. The company is actively diversifying its portfolio and investing heavily in distribution, digital channels, and a new sanitary napkin manufacturing plant to drive future growth. A notable red flag is the severe and prolonged regulatory challenges impacting the electrolyte drink category, which has hindered its performance over the past three years. └ 📄 Source

• AMRUTANJAN (Dividend): Here's an executive summary of Amrutanjan Health Care Limited's FY2025-26 annual report submission: Amrutanjan Health Care Limited reported strong performance in FY2025-26, achieving 11% revenue growth and 25% profit growth (before exceptional items), primarily driven by its pain management and women's hygiene segments. A material impact is the significant capital investment in a new sanitary napkin manufacturing plant, aimed at bolstering future growth in the women's hygiene category, alongside continued portfolio diversification and digital distribution expansion.
